label: Safe remove check
type: a default-on dependency guard that refuses to delete a backup:full-backup or backup:incremental-backup whose removal would break a later incremental backup's dependency chain, unless explicitly disabled. Present on both surfaces: cbbackupmgr's remove command (default behavior) and the REST API's DELETE-a-backup endpoint (`disable_safe_remove_check` request parameter, default `false`).
evidence: By default, the remove command will not delete backups which would cause dependencies to be broken i.e. a backup cannot be deleted if an incremental backup depends upon it.
The `disable_safe_remove_check` parameter is optional. It allows you to delete a backup that has incremental backups depending on it.
Setting `disable_safe_remove_check` to `true` can break backup cycles and make dependent backups invalid.
note: Structurally distinct from cbbackupmgr's merge command, which resolves the same full/incremental dependency by consolidation rather than a guarded deletion override - no page states the two are related, kept separate. Evidence that the full-backup/incremental-backup dependency chain (both already promoted) is a load-bearing constraint enforced independently, and identically, on both the CLI (round 19, cbbackupmgr-remove.md) and the REST surface (this round, backup-delete-backups.md).
relates_to_competency_question: What stops an administrator from deleting a backup that other backups still depend on, and can that protection be overridden?
